title: Zephyrine and the Vector
premise: Paloma Quintana has spent a decade hauling cargo through contested orbits, hiding the fact that the 'backups' sleeping in his hold are the digitized minds of colonists massacred at Meridian Station—a massacre the fleet's official records insist never happened. When the colony's children begin sharing one dream that speaks in the voices of those backups, Paloma is forced out of hiding: the dreamers are descendants of the dead, and the backups have been trying to testify for ten years. As the fleet's fragile truce expires and both factions move to erase the evidence forever, Paloma must smuggle the backups to an independent arbiter while evading the investigator assigned to him—Sera Voss, the daughter of the massacre's architect, who falls for him even as her duty demands she bury the truth. In the end, Paloma broadcasts the testimony at the cost of his ship and nearly his life; Sera chooses love and justice over inheritance, the truce collapses into a negotiated reckoning rather than war, and the children's dream finally goes quiet as the dead are named.
about_author: Ivo Thackeray is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio officer who spent six years on deep-sea freighters before turning to fiction. He writes science fiction about people who keep secrets for a living, from a harbor town whose fog he insists is load-bearing.

chapters.title: Cold Sleep Manifest
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A routine cargo inspection nearly exposes the sealed hold where forty-one backup cores sleep in stasis. He falsifies the manifest with practiced ease, but the inspector's questions linger. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of a decade of lying, and the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: Mira, a colony schoolteacher, POV. Seven children draw the same burning station and recite names no one taught them—including Mira's grandmother's. The colony council dismisses it as a fad. Emotional beat: uncanny dread blooming into reluctant hope that the dead might be speaking.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Paloma learns the fleet's ceasefire expires in ninety days, after which contested orbits become free-fire zones—and unregistered data holds become salvage. His broker urges him to wipe the cores. Emotional beat: survival instinct wrestling with a guilt he's never admitted aloud.

chapters.title: The Investigator Assigned to Me
chapters.summary: Sera Voss arrives aboard Paloma's ship under pretext of a customs audit, carrying her father's old case files on Meridian Station. She notices the mass discrepancy in his power draw. Emotional beat: two liars circling each other, each convinced they're the better actor.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. One backup core wakes unscheduled and addresses him by name: Elena Sarto, navigator of the station he once served. She asks him why he ran. Emotional beat: shame made flesh; the past stops being cargo and becomes a witness.

chapters.title: Names in Chalk
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The dreaming children lead her to a flooded sublevel beneath the colony dome where pre-colonist graffiti lists the same forty-one names. She realizes the colony was built on the massacre site. Emotional beat: vertigo of inherited complicity.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera finds the falsified manifest but sits on it, telling herself she needs more evidence. Her father's file contains a redaction order signed in his hand. Emotional beat: the first hairline fracture in her loyalty to the fleet.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Kestrel Drift
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A black-market archivist offers to authenticate the cores—for half of them, to sell as immortal slaves to the wealthy. Paloma refuses and makes an enemy. Emotional beat: discovering there are prices he won't pay, even now.

chapters.title: Shared Frequency
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira traces the children's dream to a carrier signal leaking from a passing freighter—Paloma's ship. She sends a message in the dream's own cadence, and the cores answer through every child at once. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the dead have found their mouthpiece.

chapters.title: Two Truths in One Bunk
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sera confronts Paloma; instead of arresting him, she asks what really happened at Meridian. Elena's core testifies while Sera listens, weeping without knowing why. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared horror; duty beginning to tilt.

chapters.title: The Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera decrypts her father's private ledger: orders, payment, and a line item for 'narrative management.' She records a confession she can't yet send. Emotional beat: grief for a parent who was never real, rage wearing grief's face.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Fleet marshals board the ship claiming the cores as wartime salvage before the truce lapses. Paloma jettisons decoy containers and burns hard for open space, wounded, ship crippled. Emotional beat: the invisible man finally visible, running loud.

chapters.title: The Colony Decides
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira presents the children's testimony to the colony council; half call it fraud, half call it indictment—the colonists' homes were paid for with silence. A faction votes to seize Paloma's ship themselves. Emotional beat: a community tearing along the seam of its own founding lie.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Minus Twenty-Three
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Hiding in a debris field, Paloma and Elena plan the broadcast: the independent arbiter at Cael Station will accept verified testimony, but only live, only public. Sera, officially deserter now, arrives in a stolen skiff. Emotional beat: three fugitives becoming a crew.

chapters.title: What Love Is Allowed to Cost
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera transmits her father's ledger to the arbiter as a down payment, knowing it ends her career, name, and family. Paloma tries to talk her out of it; she refuses. Emotional beat: love expressed not as comfort but as shared sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Fleet
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The children's dream spreads to spacers across three orbits—thousands hear fragments of the testimony in their sleep. The fleet declares a psychic-contamination emergency, weaponizing fear of the truth. Emotional beat: the dead's voices becoming unstoppable weather.

chapters.title: Interdiction at the Shallows
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The fleet blockades the route to Cael Station. Out of options, Paloma proposes broadcasting from inside the blockade using the ship's own beacon—an act that will paint them for every gun. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax, all three POVs interleaved. Under fire, the cores speak: forty-one voices naming the ships, the orders, the officer—Sera's father. The broadcast bleeds into every open channel. Paloma takes a hit shielding the transmitter; the ship dies around the living signal. Emotional beat: truth spoken at the exact price it always promised.

chapters.title: Arbiter
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Rescuers pull Paloma and Sera from the wreck; the arbiter authenticates the broadcast against fleet archives, exposing the redaction chain. The truce doesn't expire—it converts into mandatory arbitration. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving victory.

chapters.title: Sentencing the Living
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The tribunal names the dead publicly; the colony must reckon with its bought silence, and Mira argues for restitution over exile for the colonists' generation. Emotional beat: mercy chosen deliberately, not naively.

chapters.title: Resting State
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The cores are given the choice Elena asked for: archive, or final erasure with honors. Most choose rest. Elena thanks Paloma for carrying them, then lets go. The children's dream fades to ordinary sleep. Emotional beat: grief that is finally clean.

chapters.title: New Heading
chapters.summary: Final chapter, rotating POVs. Paloma, scarred and grounded, signs on as navigation instructor for the colony's orphaned dreamers; Sera builds the memorial archive under her own disgraced name, reclaimed; Mira teaches the children the names as history, not haunting. A new ship lifts from the colony pad. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed from burden to compass.
